Journalist Jane Pauley helms the show, taking over hosting duties from Charles Osgood, who spent 22 years on the job. A morning talk show, this program airs at a different pace and focuses much of its attention on the performing arts. After a quick update of the day's news and national weather, correspondents offer longer-length segments on a variety of topics, from architecture to ballet to music to pop culture to politics.

programme.title: BizPodcast: Why are global entrepreneurs choosing Shenzhen?
programme.desc: What makes Shenzhen such an attractive place to launch a business? With the 2026 APEC Economic Leaders' Meeting approaching, all eyes are on this innovation-driven city in China. But beyond its reputation as a tech hub, what does it actually take to turn a big idea into a real product here? In this episode of #BizPodcast, CGTN talks with two entrepreneurs about why they chose Shenzhen, how they bring ideas to market, and what young founders should know before starting a business. Would you consider starting a business in Shenzhen? What would you want to know first?

programme.desc: Global Business is the flagship business show of CGTN English Channel, bringing you the latest economic data, business trends and policies.

programme.title: Global Business-European Edition
programme.desc: Global Business is the flagship business show of CGTN English Channel, bringing you the latest economic data, business trends and policies.

programme.title: Guangdong Expands Opening Up to Connect with Asia-Pacific
programme.desc: Guangdong Province has long been one of China's pioneers in opening up. As the country's leading provincial trader, Guangdong is deepening economic ties with the Asia-Pacific through trade, innovation and closer cooperation. From coffee machines made in Shunde to robots developed through Guangdong-Hong Kong collaboration, companies are finding new opportunities across the region. The province has been China's largest provincial trader for 40 years, with last year's imports and exports topping 9 trillion yuan (about 1.3 trillion US dollars) and more than 20 million market entities. Shunde is now the world's largest coffee machine production base, with Gemilai alone shipping to over 60 countries and selling more than two million units. Leveraging the Greater Bay Area's innovation hub, Guangdong is also advancing Guangdong-Hong Kong robotics projects and, as Shenzhen hosts APEC this year, aims to deepen regional industrial and supply-chain links for shared growth.

programme.title: Shared Future for Asia Pacific: Best-selling hair dryer highlights strengths of southern China's cross-border supply chain
programme.desc: As China hosts APEC 2026, regional integration is taking center stage. In southern China's Greater Bay Area, cities like Zhuhai, Hengqin, and Macao are operating like a single supply chain network, linking automated factories with global talent and capital. To see how this cross-border teamwork helps brands go global, CGTN's Yu Hongyu takes us inside a hair dryer factory in Zhuhai.

programme.title: Shenzhen empowers Asia-Pacific with new quality productive forces
programme.desc: Once a fishing town, Shenzhen is now a city where emerging technologies move quickly from concept to daily life. Our reporter Wang Tianyu explores what powers that transformation. Take a look.

programme.title: From bikes to your phone: Carbon fiber weaves the Asia-Pacific
programme.desc: Carbon fiber-once reserved for aerospace and elite racing-is now powering a much broader industrial shift across the Asia-Pacific. In southern China, Guangdong province is turning lower-cost mass production into a major export advantage. CGTN's Yu Hongyu explores how this featherlight thread is is driving billions in APEC trade.

programme.title: OFFSHORE WIND Powers the Asia-Pacific
programme.desc: You flip a switch, and the lights come on. But where does that power come from? In Yangjiang, Guangdong, the answer lies offshore. The city leads all of China's prefecture-level cities in offshore wind capacity, backed by a growing industrial chain spanning turbine manufacturing, testing and operations. CGTN reporter Yu Bokun takes you inside China's offshore wind industry and explores how it is helping power the Asia-Pacific's green transition.

programme.title: From receptionist to manager: Elizabeth's 8-year journey at a Chinese firm
programme.desc: Elizabeth Lindon, a 46-year-old from Papua New Guinea, is now a senior supervisor at BNBM PNG in Port Moresby. Over eight years, she has worked her way up from office receptionist to forklift operator--breaking the stereotype that operating forklifts is "a man's job"--and then moving into management. Her journey shows how China-APEC cooperation translates into real benefits for individuals and families. CGTN presents a special series on the role of China's centrally administered SOEs in the Asia-Pacific, in collaboration with China's State-owned Assets Supervision and Administration Commission (SASAC). The series explores their contributions to regional connectivity, green transition, the digital economy, industrial cooperation and people's livelihoods, with insights on building a shared future for the region. #APECChina2026 #APECChinaYear

programme.title: How a Chinese company helped Danang's tofu business thrive in Indonesia
programme.desc: Pak Danang makes tofu in Mendis Village, Indonesia. He once had no license and no steady buyers -- until China Datang Power Plant stepped in with hygiene training, permits, soybeans and a supply deal with a company cafeteria. His monthly income has since jumped from IDR 12 million to 42 million ($2,300). A livelihood transformed, one block of tofu at a time. This is China-APEC cooperation made real! CGTN presents a special series on the role of China's centrally administered SOEs in the Asia-Pacific, in collaboration with China's State-owned Assets Supervision and Administration Commission (SASAC). The series explores their contributions to regional connectivity, green transition, the digital economy, industrial cooperation and people's livelihoods, with insights on building a shared future for the region. #APECChina2026 #APECChinaYear

programme.title: From 36 hours to 40 minutes: Peruvian captain's
programme.desc: Freyder Caldas Cierto ferries villagers along Peru's Huallaga River for EGH, operator of the Chaglla Hydropower Plant. Since 2015, the free community boat service has served five villages -- turning a day-and-a-half-long mule ride into a 40-minute trip. A Chinese-operated project connecting riverside lives, one trip at a time! programme.title: Mexican entrepreneur builds a China-Latin America trade bridge in the Greater Bay Area
programme.desc: Fernanda, an entrepreneur from Mexico, has launched a trade services platform in the Greater Bay Area to help Latin American companies enter the Chinese market. For her, APEC is not just a concept on paper-it is part of her everyday work, from business negotiations to cross-border partnerships. Her team also helps Chinese companies explore Latin American markets, creating new opportunities for shared growth across the Asia-Pacific.

programme.title: APEC Selfies: An Australian entrepreneur is taking AI beyond the screen. What's next?
programme.desc: From interactive smart bins to public installations that respond to emotions, Australian product designer and Sencity co-founder Steven Bai is exploring how AI can be integrated into streets, buildings and public spaces - taking technology beyond screens and into everyday life. From conceiving his startup idea to putting down roots in the Guangdong-Hong Kong-Macao Greater Bay Area, he is drawing on China's well-developed manufacturing ecosystem to bring Physical AI innovations to global markets. #APECChina2026 #APECChinaYear

programme.title: China through the eyes of CanCham Chair
programme.desc: For Dr. Mark Ceolin, Shanghai is more than a gateway to China and the Asia-Pacific - it is where his personal journey and China-Canada connections took root. Having witnessed the city’s remarkable rise since the 2000s, he has dedicated himself to helping Canadian companies grow in China. Seeing is believing. Today, Mark guides a growing number of Canadian businesses to experience a welcoming market full of emerging possibilities.

programme.title: APEC Selfies | Brewing bridges: A Filipino entrepreneur's cross-border dream
programme.desc: What happens when a Filipino coffee lover turns his passion into a business in China? Meet Diel, founder of Nearby Coffee in Quanzhou, Fujian Province, who is serving up more than just a good brew! He's building cultural connections between China and the Philippines, with plans to take his business across borders. #APECChina2026 #APECChinaYear

programme.title: APEC Selfies: Why this ROK entrepreneur wants to call China's shoe capital home
programme.desc: Entrepreneur Michael Lee from ‪the Republic of Korea‬ came to China in 2003. More than two decades later, he now calls Quanzhou in Fujian Province his home. In Jinjiang, a county-level city under Quanzhou and one of China's leading footwear manufacturing hubs, he found a world-class supply chain, constant innovation, and the opportunity to build his own business. His next big plan? To become a true local! #APECChina2026 #APECChinaYear

programme.title: BizPodcast: Why are global entrepreneurs choosing Shenzhen?
programme.desc: What makes Shenzhen such an attractive place to launch a business? With the 2026 APEC Economic Leaders' Meeting approaching, all eyes are on this innovation-driven city in China. But beyond its reputation as a tech hub, what does it actually take to turn a big idea into a real product here? In this episode of #BizPodcast, CGTN talks with two entrepreneurs about why they chose Shenzhen, how they bring ideas to market, and what young founders should know before starting a business. Would you consider starting a business in Shenzhen? What would you want to know first?

programme.title: Guangdong Expands Opening Up to Connect with Asia-Pacific
programme.desc: Guangdong Province has long been one of China's pioneers in opening up. As the country's leading provincial trader, Guangdong is deepening economic ties with the Asia-Pacific through trade, innovation and closer cooperation. From coffee machines made in Shunde to robots developed through Guangdong-Hong Kong collaboration, companies are finding new opportunities across the region. The province has been China's largest provincial trader for 40 years, with last year's imports and exports topping 9 trillion yuan (about 1.3 trillion US dollars) and more than 20 million market entities. Shunde is now the world's largest coffee machine production base, with Gemilai alone shipping to over 60 countries and selling more than two million units. Leveraging the Greater Bay Area's innovation hub, Guangdong is also advancing Guangdong-Hong Kong robotics projects and, as Shenzhen hosts APEC this year, aims to deepen regional industrial and supply-chain links for shared growth.

programme.title: Shared Future for Asia Pacific: Best-selling hair dryer highlights strengths of southern China's cross-border supply chain
programme.desc: As China hosts APEC 2026, regional integration is taking center stage. In southern China's Greater Bay Area, cities like Zhuhai, Hengqin, and Macao are operating like a single supply chain network, linking automated factories with global talent and capital. To see how this cross-border teamwork helps brands go global, CGTN's Yu Hongyu takes us inside a hair dryer factory in Zhuhai.

programme.title: Shenzhen empowers Asia-Pacific with new quality productive forces
programme.desc: Once a fishing town, Shenzhen is now a city where emerging technologies move quickly from concept to daily life. Our reporter Wang Tianyu explores what powers that transformation. Take a look.

programme.title: From bikes to your phone: Carbon fiber weaves the Asia-Pacific
programme.desc: Carbon fiber-once reserved for aerospace and elite racing-is now powering a much broader industrial shift across the Asia-Pacific. In southern China, Guangdong province is turning lower-cost mass production into a major export advantage. CGTN's Yu Hongyu explores how this featherlight thread is is driving billions in APEC trade.

programme.title: OFFSHORE WIND Powers the Asia-Pacific
programme.desc: You flip a switch, and the lights come on. But where does that power come from? In Yangjiang, Guangdong, the answer lies offshore. The city leads all of China's prefecture-level cities in offshore wind capacity, backed by a growing industrial chain spanning turbine manufacturing, testing and operations. CGTN reporter Yu Bokun takes you inside China's offshore wind industry and explores how it is helping power the Asia-Pacific's green transition.

programme.title: From receptionist to manager: Elizabeth's 8-year journey at a Chinese firm
programme.desc: Elizabeth Lindon, a 46-year-old from Papua New Guinea, is now a senior supervisor at BNBM PNG in Port Moresby. Over eight years, she has worked her way up from office receptionist to forklift operator--breaking the stereotype that operating forklifts is "a man's job"--and then moving into management. Her journey shows how China-APEC cooperation translates into real benefits for individuals and families. CGTN presents a special series on the role of China's centrally administered SOEs in the Asia-Pacific, in collaboration with China's State-owned Assets Supervision and Administration Commission (SASAC). The series explores their contributions to regional connectivity, green transition, the digital economy, industrial cooperation and people's livelihoods, with insights on building a shared future for the region. #APECChina2026 #APECChinaYear

programme.title: How a Chinese company helped Danang's tofu business thrive in Indonesia
programme.desc: Pak Danang makes tofu in Mendis Village, Indonesia. He once had no license and no steady buyers -- until China Datang Power Plant stepped in with hygiene training, permits, soybeans and a supply deal with a company cafeteria. His monthly income has since jumped from IDR 12 million to 42 million ($2,300). A livelihood transformed, one block of tofu at a time. This is China-APEC cooperation made real! CGTN presents a special series on the role of China's centrally administered SOEs in the Asia-Pacific, in collaboration with China's State-owned Assets Supervision and Administration Commission (SASAC). The series explores their contributions to regional connectivity, green transition, the digital economy, industrial cooperation and people's livelihoods, with insights on building a shared future for the region. #APECChina2026 #APECChinaYear

programme.title: From 36 hours to 40 minutes: Peruvian captain's
programme.desc: Freyder Caldas Cierto ferries villagers along Peru's Huallaga River for EGH, operator of the Chaglla Hydropower Plant. Since 2015, the free community boat service has served five villages -- turning a day-and-a-half-long mule ride into a 40-minute trip. A Chinese-operated project connecting riverside lives, one trip at a time! CGTN presents a special series on the role of China's centrally administered SOEs in the Asia-Pacific, in collaboration with China's State-owned Assets Supervision and Administration Commission (SASAC). The series explores their contributions to regional connectivity, green transition, the digital economy, industrial cooperation and people's livelihoods, with insights on building a shared future for the region. #APECChina2026 #APECChinaYear

programme.title: Dialogue at the world's largest port: Building resilient port cities together
programme.desc: How can port cities stay resilient amid global trade uncertainty? A sub-forum of the Global Mayors Dialogue in Ningbo was held at the Ningbo Zhoushan Port — the world's No.1 port in cargo throughput for 17 straight years. CGTN's Michael Wang spoke with Ningbo's Vice Mayor and guests from Cotonou (Benin), Klang Royal City (Malaysia) and Toamasina (Madagascar). Arctic shipping routes, green corridors, sister-port cooperation — the insights keep coming!

programme.title: Smart governance, shared future: How innovation is changing our cities
programme.desc: Robots that write, grasp objects and work on real production lines are becoming an everyday reality in Ningbo. How is innovation transforming our cities? From humanoid robots and smart urban governance to balancing tourism in Florence and developing a digital city atlas in Egypt, the future is already here. Learn more at this sub-forum of the Global Mayors Dialogue in #Ningbo. #Zhejiang

programme.title: Code and the kiln's glow
programme.desc: For a thousand years, Jingdezhen's kiln fires have shaped iconic ceramics and a living cultural heritage. Today, algorithms are joining the craftsmen -- helping piece together broken ceramics and give each piece a digital ID. In this episode of Living with AI, CGTN reporter He Jingyi explores how AI can help preserve ancient craftsmanship -- and how governance can keep pace when the oldest traditions meet the newest technology.

programme.title: Volkswagen aims 'In China, Beyond China'
programme.desc: Auto giant Volkswagen will bring China-developed intelligent and electrified technologies, and next-generation products to markets around the world. And China and Europe can join hands to drive the global auto transition. These are messages from Volkswagen Group CEO Oliver Blume at the #CIIE2026, as he sat down with Ralf Brandstätter, VW's China helm, for an exclusive interview with CGTN's Lily Lyu. The conversation spans tech innovation, China strategy and global auto outlook.

programme.title: China Agenda 2026
programme.desc: Special coverage of China's annual sessions of its top legislature and political advisory body, known as the "Two Sessions".

programme.title: China's concert boom: Why Gen Z is filling the stadiums
programme.desc: From packed stadium shows to sold-out performances in smaller cities, China's live music scene is expanding rapidly. Young audiences are turning concerts into a cultural routine: traveling across cities, sharing the experience online and building collective memories around live performances. The boom now extends far beyond the stage, boosting tourism, retail spending and local economies. In this episode of Unboxing China, we explore how concerts are reshaping consumption patterns and becoming a new driver of cultural and urban development.

programme.title: The self-care economy explained: How emotional spending is reshaping consumer trends
programme.desc: For months, Chinese social feeds have been filled with "Lao Ji"- a third-person way of saying "me." What began as a slang sign-off, "Love you, Lao Ji. See you tomorrow," now signals a broader shift toward self-care and emotional self-support. It also feeds a huge market where young consumers are rechanneling budgets toward small, meaningful purchases that support emotional wellbeing. In this episode of Unboxing China, we trace how a casual phrase turned into a cultural movement, reshaping consumption and mental-health talk.

programme.title: The Great Wall Homestay
programme.desc: In this episode of Travelogue, Tianran He's heading to the mountains on Beijing's northern outskirts, to meet some people his age who have swapped city life for the chance to run guesthouses beside the Great Wall of China.

programme.title: A Touch of Speed: The Art of Wing Chun
programme.desc: Uncover the principles of Wing Chun, a unique Chinese martial art renowned for its efficiency and directness. This program explores its legendary origins, core concepts like the center line theory, and its practical application in close-quarters combat. Witness the subtle power and intellectual depth of this sophisticated fighting system.

programme.title: Celebrating the Corban Festival
programme.desc: Kashgar, situated in the southwest of Xinjiang, was a key stop on the ancient Silk Road. The Corban Festival began here with the arrival of Islam in the 7th century AD, and has developed into a traditional holiday celebrated by everyone in Kashgar, just as important as Spring Festival. Locals load their tables with food to reward themselves for a year of hard work, and celebrate a tradition of sharing and generosity.

programme.title: PODCAST: When influencer culture meets ancient lakeside town - the changing face of Dali
programme.desc: Filming at a lakeside village in China's picturesque Dali prefecture, Travelogue hosts Tianran He, Jack Klumpp and Alex McCutcheon find themselves at an establishment that is two parts coffee house, eight parts photography studio, swarming with professional photographers and dedicated influencers all striving for that perfect cover photo against the shimmering Erhai Lake. They reflect on the almost mystical allure that has led travelers, past and present, to fall in love with Dali and never want to leave. Over an elegantly served Americano, they discuss how coffee production, redevelopment, and modern tourism trends are reshaping this idyllic corner of the world.

programme.title: Aerial China IV: Henan
programme.desc: Perhaps there’s no place that epitomises the cultural grandeur of China’s central plains than Henan. A cradle of Chinese civilization, abounding with resources and talented people, this is a place that has thousands of years of history in every corner. And what better opportunity to get the lowdown from on high on the cultural jewel that is Henan than by joining us on Aerial China IV…

programme.title: A Bite of China IV Ep.6
programme.desc: The fourth series of ‘A Bite of China’ takes a deep dive into seven often-overlooked culinary realms: handcrafted street snacks, local eateries, county flavors, food markets, farms, kitchens and restaurants. In short, it’s a documentary series that makes an invaluable contribution to the chronicling of China’s collective food memory.

programme.title: Gourmets Alive II Ep.1
programme.desc: Literati such as Lu You, Li Yu, Yuan Mei, and Wang Zengqi take center stage as we explore their worlds and works through the flavors and cuisine of daily life.

programme.title: Foodwise: Hangzhou Ep.1
programme.desc: In this episode Tianran and Hannah are in Hangzhou, a city with over 2000 years of history and capital of two ancient Chinese dynasties. From the famous West Lake to delicate Dragon Well tea, our hosts experience Hangzhou's must-do attractions, savouring the local cuisine and trying everything from winter melon shaped like pork belly, to food cooked according to Traditional Chinese Medicine principles, and even Buddhist noodles and Zen tea.

programme.title: Foodwise: Hangzhou Ep.2
programme.desc: In this episode, Tianran and Hannah continue their tea-tasting journey along Hangzhou's Qiantang River, exploring the region's historical culture and culinary delights. They head to Anding Mountain, enjoying misty tea at the summit. In Longmen Ancient Town, they dive into traditional Chinese clan culture and savor "Sun Quan seitan". In the gentrified village of Shishe, Hannah falls in love with "gray soup rice dumplings", while at Qiandao Lake Tianran tries the best fish head and beluga caviar he's ever had in his life. Their journey ends with a cup of Jiukeng tea and a visit to ancient tea trees.

programme.title: China Untapped: Suzhou
programme.desc: CGTN's integrated media cultural and travel program "China Untapped: Suzhou" features industrial tourism as its core theme, complemented by Jiangnan cultural tourism. The show follows a narrative thread of a foreign host touring the city alongside an international business investor. Serving as an explorer and guide, host Alex McCutcheon leads the entire industrial tour across Suzhou. UK businessman Athan Fox, acting as a potential investor and observer, views the city through the lens of commercial inspection and identifies the core strengths and investment potential of Suzhou's high-end manufacturing sector. The production team traveled across Suzhou's urban districts, Taicang, Kunshan, Changshu and other areas, visiting over 30 enterprises, research institutions and cultural tourism sites. The program presents a perfect blend of robust industrial strength and the exquisite aesthetics of Jiangnan. The two perspectives complement and validate each other, enabling global audiences to learn about Suzhou's industrial achievements and unique charm in a way that resonates with their cognitive habits.

programme.title: The Great Wall Homestay

In short, it’s a documentary series that makes an invaluable contribution to the chronicling of China’s collective food memory.

programme.title: Gourmets Alive II Ep.2
programme.desc: Literati such as Lu You, Li Yu, Yuan Mei, and Wang Zengqi take center stage as we explore their worlds and works through the flavors and cuisine of daily life.

programme.title: Foodwise: Shantou
programme.desc: Tianran and Hannah are in Shantou, Guangdong Province in south China, where they drink more tea than anywhere else in the country. They'll savor the complex aroma of the curiously named "Duck Poo Fragrance" tea, as well as enjoy a more traditional "yum cha" breakfast. They get a taste of traditional handicrafts, from breaking bowls to make inlaid porcelain to rolling "kueh" rice cakes, and feast on everything from sweet and savory street snacks to the finest seafood dining.

programme.title: Foodwise: Shaoguan
programme.desc: Tianran and Hannah are in the picturesque city of Shaoguan in Guangdong Province, South China. They try tea grown on Danxia landforms and feast on mountain produce, before getting hands-on with making rice noodles in a Hakka walled village. They learn about the Hakka people's southward migration and the effect it had on local tea and food, and end their journey in a thousand-year-old Buddhist temple, seeing how the monks integrate their practice into everyday life, and discovering just why tea is so important to Zen.

programme.title: China Untapped: Changsha
programme.desc: The city of Changsha is one of central China's powerhouses. It's a leader in both the construction machinery industry and in media - Changsha was China's first UNESCO "Creative City". It's also one of China's best-known cities for its nightlife. The soul of a city is in its people, and this episode focuses on the women of Changsha who are helping to innovate, change and further develop this city they call home.

programme.title: Brian Linden: Take me home, country roads
programme.desc: Since first arriving in China in 1984, Brian Linden has built a bond with the country that now spans more than four decades. For over 20 years, he has been rooted in Xizhou, a historic town in Yunnan. Drawn by Eastern culture, he arrived as an outsider but gradually became a dedicated rural builder. Though he has traveled to more than 120 countries, Linden ultimately chose to settle in rural southwest China. What inspired him to stay, and what China story does he hope to share with the world? Follow Linden's journey as we explore his life in rural China.

programme.title: Wudang Martial Arts & Taichi
programme.desc: Join host Yegor on a journey into the heart of China's Wudang Mountains, the spiritual cradle of Taoism, to explore the philosophy, techniques, and living spirit of Wudang Quan and Tai chi. From the internal cultivation of qi to the harmony between body and mind, Wudang martial arts are more than just physical training - they are a way of life rooted in the Tao.

programme.title: Four Faces of Muqam
programme.desc: Muqam is a performing art with its roots in the folklore of Xinjiang. Rather like an encyclopedia, Muqam is a record of the history and lifestyle of the local Uygur people. It originated in folk culture, with lyrics that covered everything from philosophical aphorisms to folk tales. Muqam is an integral part of Xinjiang culture, a vehicle for Uygur people to express their feelings and ideas.

programme.title: Sanxingdui: Rediscovering a Lost Civilisation
programme.desc: Sanxingdui Site is located at Guanghan, Sichuan Province. It is a site of an ancient city, ancient kingdom and ancient Shu culture in southwest of China, which is the largest in area, longest in time span and richest in cultural connotation. The total area covers 12 square kilometers, which was built over 3000 years ago. The cultural relics at Sanxingdui are precious cultural heritage of mankind, which contain rich historical, cultural and scientific value, and bespeak themselves as the most attractive ones amongst the multitude of the spectacular relics in China. In this episode, under the guide of the presenter, we visit the Sanxingdui Site Garden, archaeological Site and Sanxingdui Museum, show the amazing giant bronze mask, exquisite gold stuff, marvelous bronze divine tree etc., re-explore this mysterious and great civilization 3000 years ago.

programme.title: Aerial China IV: Qinghai
programme.desc: Located at the northern Qinghai-Tibet Plateau, Qinghai is home to the Three-River-Source (Yangtze, Yellow, Lancang rivers), Qaidam Basin, and Loess Plateau. Join us as we trace the history of a river from its origins in a lake, then upstream on the trail of a tiny yet adventurous fish, before reaching our destination: the boundless grasslands!

programme.title: Four Faces of Muqam
programme.desc: Muqam is a performing art with its roots in the folklore of Xinjiang. Rather like an encyclopedia, Muqam is a record of the history and lifestyle of the local Uygur people. It originated in folk culture, with lyrics that covered everything from philosophical aphorisms to folk tales. Muqam is an integral part of Xinjiang culture, a vehicle for Uygur people to express their feelings and ideas.

programme.title: Sanxingdui: Rediscovering a Lost Civilisation
programme.desc: Sanxingdui Site is located at Guanghan, Sichuan Province. It is a site of an ancient city, ancient kingdom and ancient Shu culture in southwest of China, which is the largest in area, longest in time span and richest in cultural connotation. The total area covers 12 square kilometers, which was built over 3000 years ago. The cultural relics at Sanxingdui are precious cultural heritage of mankind, which contain rich historical, cultural and scientific value, and bespeak themselves as the most attractive ones amongst the multitude of the spectacular relics in China. In this episode, under the guide of the presenter, we visit the Sanxingdui Site Garden, archaeological Site and Sanxingdui Museum, show the amazing giant bronze mask, exquisite gold stuff, marvelous bronze divine tree etc., re-explore this mysterious and great civilization 3000 years ago.

programme.title: Aerial China IV: Qinghai
programme.desc: Located at the northern Qinghai-Tibet Plateau, Qinghai is home to the Three-River-Source (Yangtze, Yellow, Lancang rivers), Qaidam Basin, and Loess Plateau. Join us as we trace the history of a river from its origins in a lake, then upstream on the trail of a tiny yet adventurous fish, before reaching our destination: the boundless grasslands!

programme.title: A Bite of China IV Ep.7
programme.desc: The fourth series of ‘A Bite of China’ takes a deep dive into seven often-overlooked culinary realms: handcrafted street snacks, local eateries, county flavors, food markets, farms, kitchens and restaurants. In short, it’s a documentary series that makes an invaluable contribution to the chronicling of China’s collective food memory.

programme.title: Gourmets Alive II Ep.2
programme.desc: Literati such as Lu You, Li Yu, Yuan Mei, and Wang Zengqi take center stage as we explore their worlds and works through the flavors and cuisine of daily life.

programme.title: Foodwise: Shantou
programme.desc: Tianran and Hannah are in Shantou, Guangdong Province in south China, where they drink more tea than anywhere else in the country. They'll savor the complex aroma of the curiously named "Duck Poo Fragrance" tea, as well as enjoy a more traditional "yum cha" breakfast. They get a taste of traditional handicrafts, from breaking bowls to make inlaid porcelain to rolling "kueh" rice cakes, and feast on everything from sweet and savory street snacks to the finest seafood dining.

programme.title: Foodwise: Shaoguan
programme.desc: Tianran and Hannah are in the picturesque city of Shaoguan in Guangdong Province, South China. They try tea grown on Danxia landforms and feast on mountain produce, before getting hands-on with making rice noodles in a Hakka walled village. They learn about the Hakka people's southward migration and the effect it had on local tea and food, and end their journey in a thousand-year-old Buddhist temple, seeing how the monks integrate their practice into everyday life, and discovering just why tea is so important to Zen.

programme.title: China Untapped: Changsha
programme.desc: The city of Changsha is one of central China's powerhouses. It's a leader in both the construction machinery industry and in media - Changsha was China's first UNESCO "Creative City". It's also one of China's best-known cities for its nightlife. The soul of a city is in its people, and this episode focuses on the women of Changsha who are helping to innovate, change and further develop this city they call home.

programme.title: Brian Linden: Take me home, country roads
programme.desc: Since first arriving in China in 1984, Brian Linden has built a bond with the country that now spans more than four decades. For over 20 years, he has been rooted in Xizhou, a historic town in Yunnan. Drawn by Eastern culture, he arrived as an outsider but gradually became a dedicated rural builder. Though he has traveled to more than 120 countries, Linden ultimately chose to settle in rural southwest China. What inspired him to stay, and what China story does he hope to share with the world? Follow Linden's journey as we explore his life in rural China.

programme.title: Back to the Land: Exploring new life in rural China
programme.desc: When we think of the countryside, what colour comes to mind? The answer lies in Wuxin - Wood, Fire, Earth, Metal and Water - an ancient rhythm that still pulses beneath China's landscapes. In this programme, we explore how the colours of Wuxing come to life through the traditions of China's ethnic minority groups. From Lugu Lake's matrilineal water world and the metal-hued fire of the Yi Torch Festival, to Dali's earth-driven crafts, Guizhou's wooden Dong dwellings, and the volcanic winds of Inner Mongolia's new nomadic life - the Five Elements guide the stories of people reconnecting with land, culture and community.

programme.title: China Untapped: Huzhou
programme.desc: Located in the east of China, on the south shore of Taihu Lake, Huzhou has been well-known for its richness in resources and blooming in silk trade since the ancient times. Guided by the concept of "lucid waters and lush mountains are invaluable assets", Huzhou now is committed to developing green industries. In this episode, CGTN hosts Tianran He and Hannah Wilson travelled to Huzhou, where they tried a variety of guesthouse hotels in the Moganshan Mountains; experienced the life of digital nomads in Anji's countryside; learned about the eco-concepts behind China's traditional architectures in Nanxun Ancient Town; and explored the development of eco-agriculture powered by high-tech along the Taihu Lake. All these phenomena demonstrate that economic development and environmental protection can achieve harmonious coexistence, and that civilization thrives if ecology is prosperous.

programme.title: Kungfu-wise: Five Ancestors Fist
programme.desc: In Quanzhou, southeast China, Kleber seeks out masters of the Five Ancestors Fist, a combination of five local kungfu styles. He meets the abbot of a Southern Shaolin Temple, and takes part in the extraordinary training regime used by Shaolin monks to hone their bodies and minds. He experiences the intricacies of Quanzhou's traditional puppetry, and learns how Five Ancestors Fist incorporated military tactics that allowed its practitioners to band together and fight off pirates.

programme.title: Wild Iberia
programme.desc: As the woods prepare to sleep and mushrooms grow as the first rains fall, flocks of cranes migrate home to Spain from their summer season in the north. The stags clash their antlers in pursuit of the does; there is little time before winter sets in.

programme.title: Destination Myanmar
programme.desc: Myanmar, also known as Burma. The Land of thousands of Golden Pagodas. Scattered like pearls around the country side. A country with some of the most beautiful scenery in Asia. Its culture and wildlife wrapped in mystique. A globally recognized biodiversity hotspot with unbroken habitats that harbor many endangered species, depicted in this tv-program ... such as the Dusky Leaf Monkey, Wild Asian Elephant, the Tapir, the Stump Tailed Macaques.

programme.title: The Rhino Orphanage: Nyani
programme.desc: The Little Nyani was born a week premature, unable to keep up with her mother, she was sent to the rhino orphanage. Raising a premature calf is a first for the orphanage. One day the little one is running around, the next she’s in Onderstepoort’s Veterinary Hospital, fighting for her life.two oldest rhinos are set to be released back into the wild. Three rhinos cause a stir as they go missing, while the younger rhinos make steady progress toward health and happiness.

Aging in the Wild
programme.desc: Reproduction is not only a concern of the young and restless: this episode of Aging in the Wild brings a light-hearted look at the issue of sexuality and camaraderie in older animals. We illustrate, for example, the link between the age of an elephant and its reproductive success. What are the reproductive benefits of these animals as they grow older? Through hearing their stories, we learn of some of the advantages - and disadvantages - of late-life reproduction.

programme.title: Wonders of the Arctic
programme.desc: Our ongoing quest to explore and come to terms with the Arctic is presented in the context of the crucial role that ice plays in the north. Ice is to the Arctic as trees are to the rainforest.

programme.title: Great White Shark - Beyond the Cage of Fear
programme.desc: Most people believe that the Great White Shark is a mindless eating machine. But what if we are wrong? In Beyond the Cage of Fear, a crew of scientists forms a relationship with a 2,000 pound Great White Shark named Bruce. They see through his eyes, swim with him, touch him and, in the end, they even attempt an experiment that most people would find absolutely crazy: introduce a Great White Shark to a real-life mermaid.

programme.title: Plastic: The Real Sea Monster
programme.desc: Plastic floats. This is where our story begins. Millions of tonnes of plastic enter the ocean every year, from rivers and shores, ships, and platforms. The world's scientists have studied the phenomenon and come to alarming conclusions.

programme.title: The Rhino Orphanage: The Hooligans
programme.desc: The orphanage is full. Cramped for space, the Hooligans inevitably begin to fight and Kalula is always in the thick of it. They desperately need a larger space. Karen travels to Kwa-Zulu Natal to inspect a new rhino orphanage, all part of her dream to create little ‘pockets of hope’.

programme.title: The Pink Panther Strikes Again (2023)

programme.title: Revenge Of The Pink Panther (2023)
programme.desc: Peter Sellers’ comedic genius shines when the hapless Inspector Clouseau is presumed to be dead.

programme.title: Easy Money (1983) (2023)
programme.desc: When boozing Monty's mother-in-law leaves him an inheritance, he must change his ways before he can collect!

programme.title: The Glory Stompers (1967)
programme.desc: When the leader of the Glory Stompers is brutally attacked by a psychotic rival biker gang that kidnaps his girl and leaves him for dead, he gathers a few buddies and sets out to settle the score! Starring Dennis Hopper, Jody McCrea and Casey Kasem.

programme.title: The Wild Angels (1966)
programme.desc: When a biker gang cyclist is injured and hospitalized, he is kidnapped from the hospital but dies. A funeral is staged in the local church with a drunken, drugged-out orgy.

programme.title: Harley Davidson And The Marlboro Man (1991)
programme.desc: Mickey Rourke and Don Johnson star in this four-lane genre collision of biker movie, heist thriller, buddy flick and sci-fi pic that will take you to the hardline of action and adventure! Co-starring Tom Sizemore, Chelsea Field and Vanessa Williams.

programme.title: Lone Wolf Mcquade (1983)
programme.desc: Chuck Norris is Lone Wolf McQuade, a Texas Ranger feared by outlaws and respected by other lawmen. When McQuade uncovers a gun smuggling operation, the action explodes, with McQuade wreaking havoc on all those who come between him and the law.

programme.title: Code Of Silence (1985)
programme.desc: Chuck Norris stars in this turbo-charged thriller that pits an honest cop against two crime lords and his own department. Henry Silva and Dennis Farina also star in a film that explodes with heart-stopping chases and martial arts confrontations.

programme.title: The Delta Force (1986)
programme.desc: Political extremists have taken innocent people hostage…and only super-soldiers Chuck Norris, Lee Marvin and The Delta Force can rescue them in this explosive adventure filled with wall-to-wall action! Martin Balsam and Shelley Winters also star.

programme.title: Delta Force 2: The Colombian Connection (1990)
programme.desc: Chuck Norris is in peak form in this explosive action/adventure that brings back one of his most unforgettable characters, Delta Force Colonel Scott McCoy, for a daring mission to destroy a deadly drug cartel led by the ruthless Billy Drago!

programme.title: American Ninja (1985)
programme.desc: Michael Dudikoff stars as Joe Armstrong, a one-man fighting machine. Serving in the army to avoid prison, Joe finds himself battling the deadly Black Star Order, as well as corrupt military leaders in order to bring down an illegal arms sale.

programme.title: American Ninja 2: The Confrontation (1987)
programme.desc: In this action-packed sequel, Joe Armstrong and Curtis Jackson are sent to the Caribbean in search of missing Marines. But they must first battle scientifically engineered Super Ninjas to bring down a dreaded drug lord known as The Lion!

programme.title: American Ninja 3: Blood Hunt (1989)
programme.desc: Martial artist David Bradley takes the reins as Sean Davidson in this third installment of the wildly popular "American Ninja" franchise, teaming up with Steve James to battle a maniacal terrorist in yet another explosive action-packed adventure!

programme.title: American Ninja 4: The Annihilation (1991)
programme.desc: Michael Dudikoff is back in action in this thrilling sequel! Teamed up with CIA operative Sean Davidson (David Bradley), Joe Armstrong (Dudikoff) returns to help foil the plans of a terrorist (James Booth) hell-bent on annihilating New York City.

programme.title: Double Impact (1991)
programme.desc: Jean-Claude Van Damme leaps into dual roles of Chad and Alex Wagner, twin brothers separated after their parents’ brutal murder. Twenty-five years later, fate reunites them and ignites their determination to exact revenge... with two times the pain.

programme.title: Bloodsport (1988)
programme.desc: In the role that kicked his international career into high gear, Jean-Claude Van Damme stars as Frank Dux, a man who refuses to lose and who might just win himself a place in history as he competes in a full-contact world championship competition.

programme.title: RoboCop (2014) (2023)
programme.desc: In 2028 Detroit, when Alex Murphy (Joel Kinnaman) -- a loving husband, father and good cop -- is critically injured in the line of duty, the multinational conglomerate OmniCorp sees their chance for a part-man, part-robot police officer.

programme.title: RoboCop (2014) (2023)
programme.desc: In 2028 Detroit, when Alex Murphy (Joel Kinnaman) -- a loving husband, father and good cop -- is critically injured in the line of duty, the multinational conglomerate OmniCorp sees their chance for a part-man, part-robot police officer.

programme.title: Hercules (2014) (2026)
programme.desc: Dwayne Johnson stars as the most towering myth of all time, revealing the man behind the legend in this bold reimaging of the famed Hercules!

programme.title: Walking Tall (2004)
programme.desc: When it comes to laying down the law, one man can make a difference! Action superstar Dwayne "The Rock" Johnson takes no prisoners as he fights for justice and crushes corruption in this story of one man who takes a stand and takes back his town!

programme.title: Walking Tall: The Payback (2026)
programme.desc: In this action-packed sequel, Kevin Sorbo discovers the quiet town he grew up in is now overrun by a violent gang. And it's up to him to take it back!

programme.title: Firewalker (1986)
programme.desc: Two hapless soldiers of misfortune (Chuck Norris, Louis Gossett Jr.) meet a beautiful girl (Melody Anderson) with a map to a lost gold mine and decide to have one last shot at striking it rich. But the trail to the treasure is no yellow brick road!

programme.title: Breaker! Breaker! (1977)
programme.desc: Breaker! Breaker! stars Chuck Norris at his butt-kicking best as a trucker on a mission to locate his kidnapped brother and bring down a corrupt Judge (George Murdock) who may just have played a role in the disappearance.

programme.title: The Octagon (1980)
programme.desc: Chuck Norris is back in this action-packed martial arts showcase co-starring the legendary Lee Van Cleef. Norris takes on his adoptive brother and a training camp where terrorists are being taught the secret killing techniques of the ninja!

programme.title: Enter The Ninja (2023)
programme.desc: When Cole (Franco Nero), a westerner trained in the deadly fighting rituals of Ninjitsu, is suddenly dragged into a dangerous dispute with an oil baron, he must face the best assassin money can buy, Ninja Hasegawa (martial arts legend Sho Kosugi)!

programme.title: Revenge Of The Ninja (2023)
programme.desc: When a band of Ninja assassins slaughters the family of Cho Osaki (Sho Kosugi), he flees to America in the hope of building a new life. Osaki tries to escape his deadly past but soon discovers he has become the pawn of a ruthless drug trafficker.

programme.title: Ninja III: The Domination (2023)
programme.desc: Possessed by the spirit of a diabolical Ninja assassin and dominated by his relentless rage, a young, attractive woman sets out to brutally attack and destroy his enemies. Can her boyfriend and a martial arts master possibly save her soul?

programme.title: Anti-Trust (2023)
programme.desc: In this sizzling, fast-paced thriller, computer whiz Milo Hoffman (Ryan Phillippe) lands his dream job at a major computer company, only to learn that the C.E.O. (Tim Robbins) may employ some very unorthodox -- and very deadly --business practices.

programme.title: Into the Blue (2005)

programme.title: Modern Marvels
programme.desc: From the earliest recorded account of an amputation and subsequent prosthesis in ancient Hindu writings, to today's use of plastics and space-age materials, we chronicle the long history of prosthetic devices.

programme.title: Modern Marvels
programme.desc: The 1969 flight of Apollo 11, which landed two American astronauts on the Moon, as seen through the eyes of the astronauts, mission controllers, engineers, and designers who made it happen.

programme.title: Modern Marvels
programme.desc: More than two million people die in the U.S. annually, creating 5,500 daily burials with 80 percent choosing caskets and 20 percent cremation; explore dealing with death throughout centuries and today's $20-billion funeral industry.

programme.title: Modern Marvels
programme.desc: Much of New York City's history can be viewed via its bridges, all 18 that connect Manhattan Island to its neighbors; the episode looks at these architectural masterpieces from the age of iron and steel and show how they have changed destinies.

programme.title: Modern Marvels
programme.desc: High-flying workers who depend on rope to do their jobs safely; how window washers, rock climbers and bungee jumpers safely use ropes; dockworkers who rely on ropes around the clock; industrial chain links.

programme.title: Modern Marvels
programme.desc: Digging up salt mining's history, from the "white gold" on the table to the oceanic and underground deposits whence it came; today people take salt for granted, but most life depends on it.

programme.title: Modern Marvels
programme.desc: Plastics are everywhere: the home, the workplace, the car, the human body, outer space, and most conspicuously, the garbage heap and landfill; join us as we review this protean substance's past and future.

programme.title: Modern Marvels
programme.desc: Explore the arch, one of humanity's strongest and most versatile structures; Romans perfected what Egyptians and Greeks experimented with, Arabs incorporated into mosques, Europeans into churches, and modern builders use in dams and future space.

programme.title: Modern Marvels

programme.title: The Civil War
programme.desc: Beginning with a searing indictment of slavery, the first episode of this series dramatically evokes the causes of the American Civil War. Here are the burning questions of Union and States' rights, John Brown at Harper's Ferry, the election of Abraham Lincoln in 1860, the firing on Fort Sumter and the rush to arms. Major figures such as Lincoln, Lee and Grant are introduced while the episode concludes with the disastrous Union defeat at Manassas, Virginia. Part 1 of 9.

programme.title: The Civil War
programme.desc: The second episode in the series begins with the political infighting that threatened to swamp Lincoln's administration and then follows Union General George McClellan's ill-fated campaign on the Virginia Peninsula, where his huge army meets a smaller but more resourceful Confederate force. The programme also focuses on Ulysses S Grant, whose exploits come to a bloody climax at the Battle of Shiloh in Tennessee, and concludes with rumours of Europe's readiness to recognise the Confederacy. Part 2 of 9.

programme.title: The Civil War
programme.desc: Convinced by July 1862 that emancipation was now morally and militarily crucial to the future of the Union, Lincoln waits for a victory to issue his proclamation. As the year wears on there are no Union victories forthcoming thanks to the brilliance of Stonewall Jackson and Robert E Lee. In September 1862 Lee invades Maryland and on the banks of Antietam Creek, the bloodiest day of the war takes place, followed shortly by the brightest: the emancipation of the slaves. Part 3 of 9.

programme.title: The Civil War
programme.desc: The fourth programme in the series reveals how the Union disaster at Fredericksburg prefaced further successes for the Confederacy. At Chancellorsville in May, Lee wins his most brilliant victory but loses Stonewall Jackson, and at Vicksburg, Grant's attempts to take the city by siege are stopped. The programme highlights the fierce Northern opposition to Lincoln's Emancipation Proclamation and ends with Lee's decision to invade the North again to draw Grant's forces away from Vicksburg. Part 4 of 9.

programme.title: The Civil War
programme.desc: This episode opens with a dramatic account of the Battle of Gettysburg in which 150,000 men fight to the death in Pennsylvania over a period of three days, culminating in Pickett's legendary charge. Also chronicled are the fall of Vicksburg, the New York draft riots, the first use of black troops, and the battles at Chickamauga, Georgia and Chattanooga. The episode closes with Abraham Lincoln in Gettysburg where he struggles to articulate what is happening to his people. Part 5 of 9.

programme.title: The Civil War
programme.desc: Episode six of the series begins with a biographical comparison of Ulysses S Grant and Robert E Lee and then chronicles the extraordinary series of battles that pitted the two generals against each other, from the wilderness to Petersburg in Virginia. In 30 days, the two armies lose more men than both sides have lost in three years of war. The programme also follows General Sherman's Atlanta campaign through the mountains of north Georgia. Part 6 of 9.

programme.title: The Civil War
programme.desc: The presidential election of 1864 sets Abraham Lincoln against his old commanding general, George McClellan. The survival of the Union itself is at stake as opinion in the North turns strongly against the war. Victories at Mobile Bay, Atlanta and the Shenandoah Valley tilt the election to Lincoln and the Confederacy's last hope for independence dies. Lee's Arlington mansion is turned into a Union military hospital and the estate becomes Arlington National Cemetery. Part 7 of 9.

programme.title: The Civil War
programme.desc: William Tecumseh Sherman's brilliant march to the sea brings the war to the heart of Georgia and the Carolinas and spells the end of the Confederacy. In March, following Lincoln's second inauguration, Petersburg and Richmond finally fall to Grant's army. Lee's tattered Army of Northern Virginia flees westward towards a tiny crossroads town called Appomattox Court House. There the dramatic and deeply moving surrender of Lee to Grant takes place. Part 8 of 9.

programme.title: The Civil War
programme.desc: The final episode of the series begins with the aftermath of Lee's surrender and then narrates the events of five days later when, on 14 April, Lincoln is assassinated. After chronicling Lincoln's poignant funeral, the series recounts the final days of the war, the capture of John Wilkes Booth and the fates of the Civil War's major protagonists. The episode then considers the consequences and meaning of a war that transformed the country from a collection of states to the nation it is today. Part 9 of 9.

The episode closes with Abraham Lincoln in Gettysburg where he struggles to articulate what is happening to his people. Part 5 of 9.
